diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, $F$ is a uniformly continuous function on $\mathcal{P}\times [0,1]$.

issues.failure_explanation: For $\T$-valued $f,g$ the expression $tf(x)+(1-t)g(x)$ is not defined on $\R/\Z$ for $t\in(0,1)$; it only makes sense after choosing real lifts, and changing the lift of $f$ at $x$ by an integer $k$ changes $F$ by $tk\bmod 1\neq 0$. The proof checks closedness separately along each loop $\gamma\in\mathcal P$ using per-loop lifts based at $O_\gamma$, but never shows that these lifts are consistent at points shared by different loops, nor that $f-g$ admits a global continuous real lift on $G$. The needed fact, that a map $G\to\T$ with zero degree on every $\partial T_w$ lifts to $\R$ (equivalently that $\mathcal P$ generates the loop structure of $G$ at every scale), is nontrivial and is not proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a lifting lemma: using uniform continuity, lift $f-g$ on each sufficiently fine cell and use that $\{\partial T_w\}_{|w|\le m}$ is a cycle basis of $\Gamma_m$ to show the local lifts patch to a continuous $h:G\to\R$; then set $F(t,x)=g(x)+th(x)$.
issues.overall_effect: The 'if' direction of Theorem thm.homotopy is unsupported, so the identification of homotopy classes of maps $G\to\T$ with degree vectors, used throughout the prose interpretation of Theorem thm.main ('unique HM in each homotopy class'), rests on an incomplete argument.
issues.title: Converse of Theorem 2.4: straight-line homotopy is not shown to be globally well defined
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and the fix is a contained but genuinely new lemma (global lifting on the SG), not a routine local edit.

issues.failure_explanation: Sections 4-7 construct one HM of prescribed degree (in detail for simple degree, by sketch for general degree). No argument is given that an arbitrary HM $f$ with data (bc-hm),(homotopy-c) coincides with the constructed one: this requires (i) a definition of harmonicity for $\T$-valued maps, (ii) showing any such $f$ lifts to a real function on the cut fundamental domain with the prescribed jumps (a lifting lemma), and (iii) showing the lift is the unique solution of the constrained discrete problems of Lemma lem.minimizer at every level. The only uniqueness statement offered (Section 6) concerns minimizers of $\hat\cE$ over $\hat H$, a different assertion whose proof is itself flawed (ISSUE-004).

issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness half of the paper's main SG theorem, and the Discussion's claim that the p.c.f. HM 'is still unique in a given homotopy class', are unsupported by the text; only existence is established (in detail for simple degree).

issues.failure_explanation: By (d-harm) a function is $\Gamma_m$-harmonic if the discrete Laplacian vanishes at every node outside $V_0$; $z_-,z_+\in V^0_m\setminus V_0$. The constrained minimizer only satisfies the combined condition $\Delta f(z_-)+\Delta f(z_+)=0$. E.g. from (Hext) with $f_{v_i}=0$, $\rho_0=1$: $f_x=-1/10$, $f_{z_-}=-1/2$, so $2f_{z_-}=-1\neq f_{v_1}+f_x=-1/10$; harmonicity fails at $z_-$. The proof of Theorem lem.ext_harmonic_on_G implicitly treats $z_\pm$ as excluded, contradicting the stated definition.

issues.overall_effect: Property 1 of Lemma lem.minimizer is false as literally stated; nothing else breaks once $\Gamma^0_m$-harmonicity is defined to exclude the cut copies.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we deduce that $\hat\cE_m(\hat f|_{V_m})$ forms a non-decreasing

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims $\hat f^*$ is the unique minimizer of $\hat\cE$ over $\hat H$. But $\hat H$ constrains only the lift increments along $\gamma_0$ and contains maps with arbitrary nonzero windings on inner loops $\gamma_i$, $i\ge1$; such maps do not restrict to elements of $H^0_m$ (real functions on the cut graph with a single jump $\rho_0$), so Lemma lem.minimizer says nothing about them. The asserted monotonicity of $\hat\cE_m$ for arbitrary $\T$-valued maps is also deduced from (E-extension), which is a statement about real-valued functions. Hence the paper establishes minimality only among maps that lift to the covering space (degree $(\rho_0)$), not over $\hat H$.

issues.failure_explanation: The entries $\rho_i$ of $\bar\omega(f)$ are indexed by loops $\gamma_i=\partial T_w$ in lexicographic order ($\gamma_4=\partial T_{11},\gamma_5=\partial T_{12},\dots$), while $\ell(w)$ weights $w_1$ least: $\ell(12)=7$ but $\partial T_{12}=\gamma_5$, and $\ell(21)=5$ but $\partial T_{21}=\gamma_7$. So (re-deg) is not a rewriting of the degree, and the gluing rule assigns the jump $\rho_{\ell(w)}$ to the cut of $T_w$, producing a map whose winding on $\partial T_w$ is a permuted entry of the prescribed vector for $|w|\ge2$. (The shift $k+\ell(w)$ in (eq:sg_gen_cuts), versus $k+\rho_{\ell(w)}$ in $H^k_m$ and the Appendix, is a further inconsistency in the same rule.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\ell$ as the lexicographic index of $w$ (or redefine $\rho_{\ell(w)}:=\omega_{\partial T_w}(f)$) and use $k+\rho_{\ell(w)}$ in the identification.
issues.overall_effect: For orders $N\ge2$ the higher-order construction as written realizes a permuted degree vector rather than the prescribed one.
issues.title: Re-indexing $\ell(w)$ in (7.2) does not match the lexicographic indexing of the degree vector

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $K$ is called a p.c.f. fractal if $V_0$ is finite.

issues.failure_explanation: $F_w^{-1}$ is applied to all of $\mathcal C$, not only to $\mathcal C\cap K_w$. Since $F_w^{-1}(c)\in K$ iff $c\in K_w$, the set contains points outside $K$, and because $F_w^{-1}$ expands, longer words produce infinitely many distinct points (for the SG, $F_1^{-1}(y)=2y-v_1\notin T$, $F_{11}^{-1}(y)=4y-3v_1$, ...). Thus $V_0$ as defined is infinite for every attractor with $\mathcal C\ne\emptyset$, so no set (not even the SG) is p.c.f. under this definition, and the scope of Section 8 is vacuous as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $F_w^{-1}(\mathcal C)$ by $F_w^{-1}(\mathcal C\cap K_w)$ (equivalently Kigami's post-critical set $\pi(\mathcal P)$).
issues.overall_effect: The formal hypothesis of Section 8 (Theorem thm.pcf and the harmonic-structure setup) is vacuous until the definition is corrected.
issues.title: Definition of the p.c.f. boundary $V_0$ omits intersection with $K$ and is never finite
issues.why_classification: A standard local correction of the definition; all subsequent statements are unaffected once made.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here, by abuse of notation $\gamma_0$ also stands for the corresponding

issues.failure_explanation: The conditions (pcf-bc-hm) prescribe increments $\partial_{v_{i-1}v_i}f$ of the lift of $f$ along arcs of the loop $\gamma_0$. The proof instead imposes $f(v_i^k)=f(v_{i-1}^k)+\delta_{i-1}$ on the cut fundamental domain. These agree only if the arc of $\gamma_0$ from $v_{i-1}$ to $v_i$ crosses no cut point $\xi(\gamma_j^{(m)})$; nothing in the postulates (cycle_extend)-(pcf-cut) guarantees this, and with the paper's own spanning-tree recipe a basis triangle's non-tree edge can lie on $\gamma_0$ (e.g. the hexagasket ring), so the lift along that arc jumps by $\rho_j$ and $\partial_{v_{i-1}v_i}f=\delta_{i-1}+\rho_j\ne\delta_{i-1}$. For the SG this was handled explicitly (the $z$-cut lies on the last arc), but no analogue is given here. In addition $\rho_0=\omega_p(f)$ uses an undefined symbol, and $\gamma_0$ (a cycle of the abstract graph $\Gamma_m$) is not given a definite realization as a loop in $K$, so the quantities in (pcf-bc-hm) are not pinned down.
